_comment: Code-scanning alerts dismissed by .github/workflows/code-scanning.yml (contrib/secops/code-scanning-triage.py). One entry per tool + rule + path glob: reason is one of 'false positive', 'won't fix', 'used in tests'; comment is the argument a reviewer can check (280 characters reach GitHub). A real finding is fixed in code, never listed here.

dismissals.comment: The 'nonce' is the wYEC burn nonce (the bridge's public replay/sequence number, plan §5), used only to pick the leader index; lock_id_mod's 0 is the n == 0 guard. Other hits are the #[cfg(test)] rotation table. No key, IV or secret.

All 5 hits are in #[cfg(test)] (module from line 273): burn nonce 9 and tx hash [0xee;32] passed to HawkeyeMemo::burn_release fixtures. The burn nonce is the bridge's public sequence number, not a cryptographic nonce.

All 6 hits are in #[cfg(test)] (from line 263): burn nonces 1/3/7/0x0102 for the burn-release memo encoding tests (plan §4). The memo's nonce is the public wYEC burn sequence number, not a cryptographic nonce.
All 6 hits are in #[cfg(test)] (from line 1454): BurnKey/replay_plan fixtures with burn nonces 0/3/4. The burn nonce is the bridge's public sequence number, not a cryptographic value.

Lines 1310/1318 pass 0 as the 'nonce' of roll::mark_unconfirmable, which only uses it as the burn number in a status text. Burn nonces are the bridge's public sequence numbers; no key, IV or secret is involved.

127: burn_unlock(peer, 0) asks a peer's /burns/unlock for burn nonce 0 to learn its responder key; 302/605: mark_orphan's nonce is only the burn number in a status text. Public bridge sequence numbers; the peer-auth nonce is random_nonce().
leader_for(0, ...) picks the slash-vote owner by rotation index 0; the parameter is named for the burn nonce (public bridge sequence number), not a cryptographic nonce.
The hit (1089) is in #[cfg(test)] (from line 1042): BurnKey::new(deployment, 7), a burn sequence number in a fixture.

Both 'password' hits (152, 164) are "pw" in the #[cfg(test)] keystore round-trip test (from line 117). Production takes the keystore password from the operator's environment variable (main.rs keys encrypt --password-env, config KeySource::Keystore).

All 8 hits are in #[cfg(test)] (from line 445): fixed [u8;16] values fed to admit_once to test the replay cache. Production request nonces come from random_nonce() (/dev/urandom, line 192, used at 400).

The peer-channel authentication golden vectors (plan §4.6): NONCE 00..0f and [0xff;16] are fixed inputs whose committed message is checked byte-exactly. Production nonces are random (hawkeye peer_auth::random_nonce).
NEAR golden-vector test: burn nonce 258 in a HawkeyeMemo::burn_release fixture; the burn nonce is the public bridge sequence number.

Store tests (events, migrations, reorg, sign_once, transitions): every one of the 65 hits was read and is a burn sequence number (burn_key(n), new_burn(n,..), BurnKey::new(dep,n), matcher_burn/adopt_release nonce) in a fixture.
Integration tests (bond_exit.rs, engine.rs): all 6 hits were read and are burn sequence numbers (BurnKey::new, burn_release memo nonce 77, burn_unlock(url, 5), held_body(0,..)) in regtest fixtures.

The URL is the operator's own [ycash] rpc_url from the config file (config.rs, transport-checked by credentials_safe: loopback or TLS unless allow_insecure_rpc), set once at start; no part comes from a peer, the API or chain data.
Prints the JSON outcome: account id, public key text and the key file path. The secret key is only written to the --out file, never printed. near-admin is a devnet set-up helper.
panic!("{e:?}") of unexpected error variants in mock-RPC tests; the 'sensitive' value is a NEAR account id (public), no key material.
Sandbox test output: gas figures, scan heights and events, the relayer account id (public NEAR account names). No key material is printed.
The assert! message prints the JSON body returned by the test's own local Hawkeye API (regtest engine test); no operator log is written.
